focus.label: Posterior circulation stroke
focus.why: Neck rotation supports vertebrobasilar mechanism; cerebellar signs support central lesion; low risk and CSF changes are atypical.

payload.query: Need brain MRI with DWI and MR angiography of posterior circulation to confirm or exclude acute cerebellar/brainstem infarction, plus CSF cell count and microbiology results to assess CNS infection; these are core for differentiating the two leading hypotheses.

payload.analysis: Combined with the suspicion of posterior circulation stroke, MRI reveals multiple acute infarcts in left thalamus, occipital lobe, and cerebellum, and CTA shows fenestration of the left vertebral artery; cardiac and autoimmune workups are negative, supporting an arteriopathic/embolic mechanism rather than cardioembolic or inflammatory cause. CSF cell counts are normal, further favoring stroke over CNS infection. All key imaging information is covered.

why.why: MRI shows multiple acute infarcts in the left thalamus, occipital lobe, and cerebellum, directly confirming posterior circulation stroke. CTA demonstrates fenestration of the left vertebral artery, and negative cardiac/autoimmune workups with normal CSF cell counts favor an arteriopathic/embolic mechanism over cardioembolic, inflammatory, or infectious causes. Confidence raised from 0.35 to 0.90.

payload.analysis: 结合急性眩晕、呕吐、步态不稳及Romberg征，MRI示左丘脑、左枕叶、左小脑多发急性梗死，CTA示左椎动脉V2-V3段开窗畸形，心脏超声和动态心电图未见异常，自身免疫、感染及CSF细胞数均正常，支持后循环卒中，机制倾向动脉病/栓塞。CSF压力和蛋白轻度升高但细胞数正常，不支持感染/炎症或原发性颅高压，周围性眩晕由中枢梗死排除。所有关键影像及实验室信息已覆盖，诊断明确，建议按后循环卒中管理。

payload.report: 36-year-old man without vascular risk factors developed acute dizziness, vomiting, and gait instability 6 hours after extreme head rotation, with central signs (left limb ataxia, positive Romberg). Normal CSF cell count and negative cardiac/autoimmune workups excluded infection and cardioembolism. MRI confirmed acute infarcts in the left thalamus, occipital lobe, and cerebellum; CTA showed left vertebral artery V2-V3 fenestration. This establishes posterior circulation stroke due to vertebral arteriopathy.
